blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Ratio represents a quantitative comparison between two quantities of the same unit.
Ratio in fractions requires clearing denominators by finding their LCM to simplify into whole numbers.
Proportion establishes the equality of two ratios, where the product of means equals the product of extremes.
Compound ratio is calculated by multiplying the antecedent terms together and consequent terms together.
Distribution problems involve dividing a total quantity into parts directly proportional to given ratios.
A ratio is a comparison of two quantities of the same kind.

Ratio of a and b = a : b

Example:

Ratio of 10 and 20 = 10 : 20 = 1 : 2
When two ratios are equal, they form a proportion.

a : b = c : d

This can also be written as:

a × d = b × c

In SSC examination, questions from this topic are:

• Direct

• Formula-based

• Mostly numerical

blocks.content:
• Ratio has no unit.

• Both terms must be of the same unit.

• Ratio can be simplified like fractions.

• Ratio remains same if both terms are multiplied or divided by the same number.

Example 1:

Find the ratio of 45 minutes to 1.5 hours.

Solution:

1.5 hours = 90 minutes

45 : 90 = 1 : 2

Answer: 1 : 2

If a : b = c : d, then:

a × d = b × c
Compound ratio is the ratio obtained by multiplying corresponding terms of two or more ratios.

Example 5:

Divide ₹600 between A and B in the ratio 2 : 3.

Solution:

Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5

A’s share = (2/5) × 600 = 240

B’s share = (3/5) × 600 = 360

Answer: A = ₹240, B = ₹360

• Convert all quantities to the same unit.

• Simplify ratios to lowest form.

• Use proportion formula carefully.

• Ratio questions are often combined with percentage.

items: Questions on Compound Ratio and Proportion are frequently tested in tier-1 competitive exams.
Pay special attention to Ratio in Distribution Problems as they are key to solving partnership and age-related questions.
Always simplify fractional ratios into standard whole number ratios before applying distribution formulas.

blocks.content:
Example 6:

The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 2. If there are 30 boys, find the number of girls.

Solution:

3 : 2 = 30 : x

x = 20

Answer: 20



Example 7:

If a : b = 5 : 7 and b : c = 14 : 15, find a : c.

Solution:

a : b = 10 : 14

b : c = 14 : 15

a : c = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3

Answer: 2 : 3
